info.title: Neighborhood Commons API
info.description:
The Neighborhood Commons API: typed substrate for neighborhood-scale public facts. Schema.org-aligned types (Place, Organization, Person, Event, Broadcast, List), verification + reputation system, opt-in filter primitives. Read free, write through verified app integrations. CC BY 4.0.

**This document is the Spec, part of the Commons Contract.** The Contract is three files together: the Spec (this document — machine-readable, authoritative), the Guide (`/llms.txt` — narrative companion), and the Log (`CHANGELOG.md` — dated record of every change). Rule when they disagree: Spec wins. Guide explains. Log dates.

**1.0.0 commits** to additive-only stability. Future minor versions add types, fields, or endpoints without breaking existing consumers. Breaking changes require 2.0.0 and very strong justification.

get.description: Published events, paginated and filtered. No authentication required.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Text search across name and description

parameters.name: near
parameters.description: Coordinates as lat,lng for proximity filtering

parameters.name: collapse_series
parameters.description: Deduplicate series to nearest upcoming instance

parameters.name: series_id
parameters.description: Filter to events in a specific series

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: Filter to events belonging to a specific group

parameters.name: tmdb_id
parameters.description: Filter to all showings of a film (clusters film-category events across theaters and dates). Pair with `?category=film` for clean results.

parameters.name: first_party
parameters.description: Filter by authorship tier. `true` = events posted by the verified business itself (first-party). `false` = events aggregated from public sources (scrapers, feeds, ingestion pipelines). Omit for both. The Commons separates information *from* a business from information *about* a business; apps choose what tier to surface.

servers.description: Changes feed lives OUTSIDE the /v1 prefix. Full URL: https://api.neighborhood-commons.org/api/events/changes

get.description: Lightweight public sync endpoint for consumers without a service key. Returns events whose updated_at is greater than the `since` cursor, plus the IDs of events that have ended since that cursor. NOT under /v1 — the full URL is `/api/events/changes`. Rate limit: 10/min per IP. Responses are cached 60s. For higher throughput, use a service key and call `/v1/service/events`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Returns events updated after this point.

sync_cursor.description: Pass this as the next request's `since` value.

has_more.description: If true, another page of changes exists — call again with the returned sync_cursor.

get.description: Single event by ID in Neighborhood API format.
iCalendar feed of events. Accepts the same query filters as /events. Default window: 30 days ago to 90 days ahead. Series are deduplicated with RRULE.
RSS 2.0 feed of events. Accepts the same query filters as /events. Supports pagination via limit/offset.

200.description: Feed name, stewards, license, and supported resources

get.description: Geographic regions with timezone and center coordinates. Cached for 1 hour.
Categories with current event counts. Sorted by count descending. Cached for 30 minutes.
Live counts of published events, active venues, and primary region. No authentication required. Cached for 5 minutes.

post.description:
Subscribe to event changes. Returns the signing secret once — store it securely. Webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256. Max 5 subscriptions per API key.

**Event types:** `event.created`, `event.updated`, `event.deleted`, `event.series_created`, `event.image_processed`. The default subscribes to the first four; `event.image_processed` is opt-in (different payload shape — see Guide for details).

url.description: HTTPS endpoint. Must resolve to a public IP (RFC 1918 and cloud metadata addresses blocked).

event_types.description: Event types to subscribe to. Defaults to all event.* types except `event.image_processed`, which has a different payload shape and must be opted into explicitly.

201.description: Subscription created. The signing_secret is returned only on creation — it cannot be recovered later.

signing_secret.description: 64-character hex secret for HMAC-SHA256 verification. Shown once.

400.description: Invalid URL or URL validation failed (SSRF protection). Error codes: INVALID_WEBHOOK_URL

409.description: Subscription limit reached (max 5 per API key)

get.description: List all webhook subscriptions for the calling API key.

patch.description: Update the URL, event types, or status (active/paused) of a webhook subscription.

403.description: Webhook belongs to a different API key

delete.description: Delete a webhook subscription. Future events will not be delivered to this endpoint.

403.description: Webhook belongs to a different API key

post.description: Send a test payload to the webhook endpoint. Useful for verifying signature verification logic.

403.description: Webhook belongs to a different API key

get.description: Recent delivery attempts for a webhook subscription, newest first. Filter by `status` and/or `event_id` to confirm a specific event reached this subscriber — useful for reconciling missed deliveries without a full re-scan.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter to a single delivery state.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Filter to deliveries for a specific event UUID. Combine with `status=delivered` to confirm a specific event landed.

event_type.description: The event_type that triggered this delivery (e.g. `event.created`, `event.image_processed`).

event_id.description: The event UUID this delivery is for.

status_code.description: HTTP status code returned by the subscriber endpoint, or null if no response was received.

error_message.description: Failure reason (truncated to 500 chars). Null on success.

next_retry_at.description: When the next retry will fire. Null on terminal states.

403.description: Webhook belongs to a different API key

get.description: List events with full internal fields. Supports filtering by status, time, category, search, and source method. By default shows one-offs + first instance of each series; pass all_instances=true for reconciliation.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Text search on title, venue name, address

post.description: Create a single or recurring event on behalf of a linked account. Uses Neighborhood API friendly-shape field names (name, start, timezone, location, url, cost) — symmetric with GET /events responses. Omit recurrence for one-off events. For recurring events, creates a full series and returns series_count and instance_ids.

403.description: NOT_LINKED — service key not linked to account

patch.description: Bulk-update up to 200 events by ID. Only updates provided fields. Scoped to accounts linked to this key (admin keys bypass).

403.description: NOT_LINKED for one or more events

get.description: Get a single event with full internal fields and account info.

patch.description: Update a single event. Scoped to accounts linked to this service key.

delete.description: Delete a single event. Scoped to accounts linked to this service key.

patch.description: Update all future instances of a recurring series. Scoped to accounts linked to this service key.

delete.description: Delete all future instances of a recurring series. Scoped to accounts linked to this service key.

post.description: Upload an image for an event. Image is re-encoded through Sharp (JPEG/PNG/WebP only, max 12MB). Returns the CDN URL.

400.description: Invalid image type or corrupt file

get.description: Detailed stats: account counts (total, claimed, pending), event counts, and category distribution. Admin service key required.
List all API keys with event contribution stats. Admin service key required.

post.description: Create a new API key. The key is the credential; the `account_id` it links to is the stable owner of any events it creates. Rotation: issue a new key with the same `account_id` as the old one, then revoke the old key — both keys can edit the same events while both are active. Non-service tiers REQUIRE `account_id` (without a linked account, PATCH/DELETE on created events would fail with KEY_NOT_LINKED). Returns the raw key string ONCE — store it immediately, it is unrecoverable.

account_id.description: Required for non-service tiers. The portal_account that owns events created with this key.

201.description: Key created. The `key` field is the raw secret — store it immediately.

key.description: The raw API key — pass as X-API-Key. Returned ONCE; not recoverable.

400.description: Validation error or ACCOUNT_REQUIRED for non-service tiers without account_id

patch.description: Update an API key's name, URL, status, contributor_tier, or contact_email. Admin service key required.

post.description: Flip a self-registered service-tier API key from pending (`activated_at` NULL — reads only) to fully active (`activated_at` set — writes resume). Optionally sets `brand_config`, `verification_authority`, and `rate_limit_per_hour` in the same call. Admin service key required. Idempotent: returns `already_active: true` if the key was previously activated.

brand_config.description: Per-key sender identity for verification emails. Operator-set at activation.

verification_authority.description: Methods this key may auto-approve, e.g. ["manual_review:in_person"].

post.description: Step 1 of self-issuance for a service-tier API key. Sends a verification code to the supplied email. Step 2 is `POST /service/register/verify-otp`, which issues the (pending) key. No authentication required.

post.summary: Self-service: verify OTP and receive a pending service key
post.description:
Step 2 of self-issuance. On a valid OTP, creates a service-tier api_key with `activated_at = NULL` and stores the application metadata for review. The raw key is returned ONCE — store it immediately.

The issued key authenticates for reads at the service-tier rate limit and for the `/service/verifications/path` lookup, but every write under `/service/*` returns `403 KEY_PENDING` until an admin calls `POST /service/api-keys/{id}/activate`. No code changes needed when the key is activated.

what_youre_building.description: One paragraph. Who's the user, what's the integration shape.

verification_process.description: How you verify the organizations you onboard. Drives the verification_authority granted at activation.

raw_key.description: Returned once. Store immediately — not recoverable.

409.description: An active service-tier key already exists for this email (ALREADY_EXISTS)

post.description: Rewrites image URLs across portal_accounts and events to direct R2 public URLs. Converts portal proxy paths and re-hosts external URLs (Google Places, gstatic, etc.) through the Sharp pipeline. Admin service key required. Requires `R2_PUBLIC_URL` to be configured on the server. Idempotent — safe to re-run.

get.description: List domains on the Contribute API allowlist. Admin service key required.

post.description: Add a domain to the Contribute API allowlist. Resolves any pending approval request for the same domain. Admin service key required.

domain.description: Lowercase hostname only — no scheme, port, or path.

delete.description: Remove a domain from the allowlist. Future Contribute API submissions for this domain will queue for review. Admin service key required.

get.description: Review queue of Contribute API URL submissions whose domain is not yet on the allowlist. Admin service key required.

post.description: Add the requested domain to the allowlist and mark the request approved. Admin service key required.
Mark the request rejected without allowlisting the domain. Admin service key required.

get.description: Public read of Place records (physical locations). Filter by region, geo proximity, or text search. No firehose: at least one structural filter recommended.

parameters.name: near
parameters.description: Coordinates as lat,lng for proximity filtering

get.description: Public read of Organization records. Filters compose for opt-in consumption: `kind` for subtype, `verified` and `verified_by` for trust, `near`/`radius_km` for proximity, `created_by_contributor` for app-source slicing.

parameters.name: verified
parameters.description: True to filter to verified organizations only.

parameters.name: verified_by
parameters.description: Comma-separated app names. Filters to organizations verified by any of these apps.

parameters.name: not_verified_by
parameters.description: Comma-separated app names. Excludes organizations verified by these apps.

parameters.name: created_by_contributor
parameters.description: Filter to organizations created by accounts linked to this contributor app.

get.description: Public read of Person records (DJs, performers, curators, individual organizers).

Public read of active Broadcast records (ephemeral signals from organizations, pinned to places). Returns active-only by default; `near`+`radius_km` is the typical proximity filter. Apps surface broadcasts editorially — verification is a filter, not a Commons-side gate.

parameters.name: verified
parameters.description: Filter to broadcasts from verified organizations.

get.description: Public read of List records (curatorial selections of events, organizations, or places).

Public read of the verifier registry. Each entry summarizes one app's verification track record (count, active, revoked, methods). Apps reading the Commons can use this to compose verified_by filters that match their trust policy.
Public spot-check of recent approvals issued by a specific verifier app. Maximum sunlight on the reputation graph — anyone can audit who's being verified by whom.
Routing authority. Given a target and identifier, the Commons returns which submission endpoint to call next. Apps must call this first and follow the result — submission endpoints reject mismatches.

post.description: Auto-track verification path: send a one-time code to the identifier (email). Used for business-domain emails on heavy-rigor org targets, or any email on light-rigor targets (groups, persons). Personal-email domains for heavy-rigor targets are rejected here with WRONG_METHOD — call /service/verifications/manual instead.

201.description: Challenge created; email sent (with the calling key's brand_config sender identity)

409.description: WRONG_METHOD — this identifier requires the manual review path. Response includes redirect hint.

post.description: Submit the one-time code received via email. On match: an entry is added to the target's verified identifiers. On miss: attempt counter increments; challenge expires after configured limit.

Manual-review path: app submits structured evidence for human review. Required evidence schema is Commons-defined and validated at submit. Apps with `verification_authority` for the matching method auto-approve on submit; others queue for admin review.

For heavy-rigor org targets, this is the path for personal-email domains. For light-rigor targets, this path is rarely used (challenges suffice).

200.description: Verification outcome — verified (auto-approved by app authority), pending (queued), or rejected.

409.description: WRONG_METHOD — this identifier should use the challenges path.

get.description: Admin-tier read of the manual review queue. Only callers whose service key has `is_admin=true` (or has `verification_authority` covering the relevant method) see results.

post.description: Admin or authorized-app action. Inserts the verified identifier and marks the review approved. Approval criteria documented in `docs/verification-policy.md` — reviewer is bound by Commons-defined floor.
Admin or authorized-app action. Records the rejection with a Commons-defined reason code. Rejection is a permanent record but doesn't prevent future fresh submissions for the same identifier.
v1 minimum: stores a dispute claim against a verified target or identifier for operator review. No automated action. Acts as the entry point for "this verification is wrong" feedback into the system.

post.summary: Create or look up a place
post.description: Idempotent on `googlePlaceId`: if a Place with that external ID exists, returns it instead of creating a duplicate. Without a googlePlaceId, creates a new Place row from the provided fields.

200.description: Existing place returned (idempotent match on googlePlaceId)

patch.description: Service-tier callers can update organizations linked to their key (via api_key_account_links). Admin keys bypass the scoping check.

post.description: Create an ephemeral signal pinned to a Place. The Organization must be linked to the calling key (via api_key_account_links) unless the key has admin privileges. Verification is NOT required at create time — apps filter on verified status when surfacing.
Marks the broadcast retracted. Status changes to `retracted` and `retracted_at` is set. Idempotent.

403.description: Not linked to the curator entity

patch.description: Updates list name/description/slug. Items are managed via /service/lists/{id}/items endpoints.

403.description: Not linked to the curator entity

post.summary: Add an item to a list
post.description: Adds an event, organization, or place to the list at the specified position. If position conflicts with existing items, behavior is configurable (default: shift existing items down).

403.description: Not linked to the curator entity

delete.summary: Remove an item from a list

403.description: Not linked to the curator entity

post.summary: Link an existing organization to this service key
post.description: Establishes a relationship between the calling service key and an existing Organization. After linking, the key may write to that organization's data (events, broadcasts, identifier verifications, lists curated by it). Idempotent: calling on an already-linked organization returns 200 with the existing link.
Multipart upload. Validates magic bytes, re-encodes through Sharp, stores in R2. Updates organization.logo to the new URL.

200.description: Logo uploaded; new URL written to organization.logo

post.description: Multipart upload of a hero/cover image. Same pipeline as logo upload. Updates organization.image.

200.description: Image uploaded; new URL written to organization.image

patch.description: Set or remove the organizer of an event. Organizer is exactly one of an Organization or a Person. Pass nulls for both to clear (rare — events generally must have an organizer). Scoped to events whose current organizer is linked to the calling key.

403.description: Not linked to this event or its current organizer

open_window.description: True for come-and-go events (happy hour, open swim, market). When true, feeds keep the event visible until end_time (or start + 3h if no end). When false, the event disappears from feeds at start time.

capacity.description: Informational max attendance. Commons does NOT track signups or enforce the cap. Ticketing lives in url.

rsvp.description: Whether RSVP is a thing for this event. Commons does not manage RSVPs.

series_instance_count.description: Total instances in the series. Populated on /events and /events/{id}. Null for one-offs or in contexts where hydration is skipped (webhook payloads).

first_party.description: Whether the event was entered by its originator (venue, host, group) rather than a third party

event_image_focal_y.description: Vertical focal point for image cropping (0=top, 1=bottom, 0.5=center)

tmdb_id.description: TMDB film ID (themoviedb.org), used to cluster film-category events across theaters and dates. Recommended when category includes 'film'. Format: numeric string (e.g. '1064713' for Anora). Consumers fetch metadata at https://api.themoviedb.org/3/movie/{tmdb_id}. Films not in TMDB leave this null and appear individually instead of clustering. Filterable on `GET /events?tmdb_id={id}`.

contributor.description: The app that contributed this data to the commons. Null for portal-submitted events.

ServiceEvent.description: Event response shape for service-tier and portal endpoints. Uses DB-flavored field names (title, event_date, start_time, etc.) — distinct from the public read Event shape. Returned by GET /service/events/{id}, PATCH /service/events/{id}, and the portal API.

title.description: Equivalent to `name` in the public Event shape

venue_name.description: Equivalent to `location.name` in the public Event shape

category.description: Single category slug (the public Event shape wraps this in an array)

recurrence.description: iCal RRULE string, or null for one-offs

price.description: Equivalent to `cost` in the public Event shape

ticket_url.description: Equivalent to `url` in the public Event shape

tmdb_id.description: TMDB film ID for clustering film-category events. See Event.tmdb_id.

ServiceAccount.description: A portal account as seen by service-tier callers — includes internal fields. Retained in 1.0.0 because GET /service/events/{id} still returns the linked account; the dedicated /v1/service/accounts/* paths are removed.

url.description: The full URL that triggered the review

ServiceEventInput.description: Input schema for the Service API. Uses Neighborhood API friendly-shape field names (name, start, location, url, cost) — symmetric with the read schema. Recurrence is optional; omit for one-off events.

image_url.description: Source image URL; fetched, re-encoded through Sharp, and hosted by Commons.

recurrence.description: RRULE string (e.g. FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=12). Omit for one-off events.

open_window.description: True for come-and-go events. Default false.

capacity.description: Informational only; Commons does not enforce.

rsvp.description: Whether RSVP is a thing for this event. Commons does not manage RSVPs.

contributor.description: Per-event attribution for the app/tool that publishes this event, distinct from the account-derived source.publisher. Surfaces on the read path as source.contributor. Omit to fall back to legacy derivation (source.publisher on api-method events). Send null on PATCH to clear an existing override.

tmdb_id.description: TMDB film ID for clustering film-category events. Send numeric string (e.g. '1064713') when category includes 'film'. See Event.tmdb_id for the read-side semantics.

ErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable error identifier. Groups:

- **Auth**: `ACCESS_DENIED`, `ACCOUNT_DISABLED`, `ACCOUNT_REQUIRED`, `API_KEY_REQUIRED`, `CAPTCHA_FAILED`, `FORBIDDEN`, `INSUFFICIENT_TIER`, `INVALID_API_KEY`, `INVALID_OTP`, `KEY_NOT_LINKED`, `KEY_PENDING`, `NOT_LINKED`, `NO_OWNER`, `UNAUTHORIZED`
- **Validation / resource**: `ALREADY_EXISTS`, `BATCH_ALREADY_SUBMITTED`, `CONFLICT`, `DUPLICATE`, `INVALID_STATE`, `NOT_FOUND`, `VALIDATION_ERROR`
- **URL / domain**: `BLOCKED_HOSTNAME`, `DOMAIN_PENDING_REVIEW`, `INVALID_SCHEME`, `INVALID_URL`, `INVALID_WEBHOOK_URL`, `IP_LITERAL`, `URL_CREDENTIALS`
- **Rate limit / quota**: `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `RATE_LIMIT`, `SUBSCRIPTION_LIMIT`
- **CSV / import**: `CSV_EMPTY`, `CSV_INVALID`, `CSV_TOO_LARGE`, `NO_VALID_ROWS`
- **Verification**: `IDENTIFIER_DISPUTED`, `IMPOSTER_SIGNALS`, `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, `OUT_OF_POLICY`, `WRONG_METHOD`
- **Server / infrastructure**: `DATABASE_ERROR`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `SERVER_ERROR`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `UPSTREAM_ERROR`

PostalAddress.description: Schema.org PostalAddress. Used to represent structured addresses on Place and related types.

IdentifierValue.description: Schema.org PropertyValue used in identifier arrays. Carries external IDs (e.g., googlePlaceId) alongside our internal UUIDs.

OpeningHoursEntry.description: Schema.org OpeningHoursSpecification entry. One per day-range. Times are 24h HH:MM in the entity's local timezone.

dayOfWeek.description: Single day or array of days. Schema.org-canonical: full names.

Place.description: Schema.org Place. A physical location. Identity is the address; verification is implicit via googlePlaceId resolution.

identifier.description: External IDs. Common entry: { propertyID: "googlePlaceId", value: "ChIJ..." }

region_slug.description: Slug of the region this place falls within, if any

PlaceInput.description: Input for /service/places. Idempotent on googlePlaceId: if a Place with that ID already exists, returns it instead of creating a duplicate.

Verification.description: Verification block exposed on verified Organization or Person responses. Public read includes method, verification time, and approving app — the reputation graph is intentionally transparent.

verifiedByApp.description: Stable app name (snapshot at approval time, immune to key rotation).

VerifiedIdentifier.description: A specific verified identifier on a target. Service-tier responses include full value; public responses may mask.

identifierValue.description: Full value for service-tier reads; null or partial for public reads.

Organization.description: Schema.org Organization. Discriminated by `kind`: `local_business` and `business` are heavy-verification subtypes; `community_group`, `nonprofit`, `curator`, `collective` use light verification (control of identifier).

legalName.description: Official registered name. Optional, primarily for verified businesses.

additionalType.description: Schema.org type URL aligned with kind (e.g., https://schema.org/LocalBusiness, https://schema.org/NGO, https://schema.org/Organization).

sameAs.description: URLs that unambiguously identify this organization (Wikipedia, Wikidata, social profiles).

location.description: The Place this Organization primarily operates at. Null for organizations without a fixed location (touring, online-only).

slug.description: Optional; auto-generated from name if omitted.

primaryPlaceId.description: Reference to a Place row. Required for kind=local_business; optional otherwise.

Person.description: Schema.org Person. Used for individuals — DJs, performers, curators, individual organizers. Light verification (control of email).

Broadcast.description: Ephemeral real-time signal from an Organization, pinned to a Place. Maximum lifetime 24h. No direct Schema.org analog; conventions borrowed from SpecialAnnouncement (`datePosted`, `expires`).

expires.description: Must be in the future and within 24h of now.

ListItem.description: Schema.org ListItem. Used inside ItemList.itemListElement to pair an item reference with its position and an optional curator note.

item.description: The referenced entity. The shape matches the corresponding type's schema; consumers can discriminate on the schema or by looking at fields.

curatorNote.description: Curator's optional commentary on this item.

List.description: Schema.org ItemList. A curatorial selection by an Organization or Person — "this weekend's picks," "best park benches in Fishtown," etc.

curator.description: The Person or Organization that maintains this list.

Verifier.description: Reputation-graph entry. One per app that has ever issued a verification.

approvalCount.description: Total approvals issued by this app, ever.

methods.description: Methods this app has approved with (e.g. "manual_review:in_person").

VerifierApproval.description: An approval by a verifier, surfaced for spot-checking on the reputation graph.

VerificationPathResponse.description: Result of /service/verifications/path. The Commons dictates which submission endpoint to call next; apps follow.

alreadyVerified.description: True if this exact (target, identifier) pair is already verified.

endpoint.description: Path of the submission endpoint to call next.

code.description: One-time code delivered via verification email.

VerificationOutcome.description: Result of a verification submission. Status `verified` means the row landed in account_verified_identifiers; `pending` means manual review queued; `rejected` means the submission failed policy.

reviewId.description: Set when status=pending; reference for tracking.

VerificationManualInput.description: Submission for the manual-review path. Evidence is structured and required fields enforced at submit. Apps with verification_authority for the matching method auto-approve; others queue.

reviewerAccountId.description: Identifier of the human reviewer who attests.

PendingReview.description: An item in the verification review queue (admin-tier endpoints).

DisputeInput.description: Records a dispute against a verified target, identifier, or other data record. v1 stores for operator review only — no automated action.

submitterContact.description: Optional email or phone for follow-up.

ValidationError.description: Request payload or query parameters failed validation

browseApiKey.name: X-API-Key
browseApiKey.description: Optional for read endpoints (higher rate limit bucket). Required for webhook management.

serviceApiKey.name: X-API-Key
serviceApiKey.description: Service-tier API key. Scoped: can only modify data for accounts linked to this key. Admin keys bypass scoping.
